Olyshivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Olyshivka's earliest known Jewish community was established in the second half of the 19th century; Jews were involved in trade, owning five shops including three grocery stores. The community survived a pogrom in 1919, though by 1920 Jews made up just 0.1 percent of the population; only 29 Jews remained by 1939. This cemetery, likely marked on Russian maps from the 1870s, still existed according to local residents in the first half of the 20th century, though no visible traces or boundaries survive today.
